subject: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy

Olivia — following up from our call this morning. Attached is our near-final MSA + the one-page order form with the standard commercial redlines. Two items NorthBridge flagged on the call we want to make sure we resolve now so procurement can sign:

1) Limitation of liability: our position is a monetary cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
2) SLA / service credits: credits are designed to be a mitigation/limited remedy for availability incidents; they are capped and expressly not a monetary damages substitute. We typically keep a "sole remedy" carve only for SLA credits (i.e., credits are the exclusive remedy for SLA breaches) but do not let that erode the liability carve-outs.

Please review the attached redline (MSA_redline_karthik_20260512.pdf). If your legal team has specific alternate language, would appreciate a tracked change pass so we can evaluate quickly. Our goal is to preserve customer protections while not exposing Redwood to uncapped consequential exposure.

Next steps: please share NorthBridge's redline by EOD tomorrow (5/13) and we'll route to Legal (cc Laura & Neha) for a fast turnaround. If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call with legal tomorrow.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@northbridge.ai>

Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy

Karthik — thanks for the redline and the call recap. Attached is NorthBridge's counter with comments. High-level asks from our counsel:

- Removal of liability cap for damages arising from breach of confidentiality, privacy/data protection, and willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages excluded generally, but they want an explicit carve that allows recovery for aggregated loss resulting from Data Loss (they'd prefer "no exclusion for direct losses arising from loss of Customer Data").
- SLA credits: they want credits to be a "sole and exclusive remedy" for downtime and performance issues; they are worried that Redwood could be liable for additional consequential damages even after credits.

We added tracked changes in NorthBridge_counter_20260513.pdf. Marcus (cc'd) is NorthBridge's procurement lead and will track internal approval. We can jump on a call if helpful but prefer redline-first.

Olivia
Director, Strategic Partnerships — NorthBridge AI
Attachment: NorthBridge_counter_20260513.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy

Looping legal — NorthBridge pushed hard on removing caps for privacy/data loss and wants credits to be sole remedy. Procurement (Marcus) is pushing to close this week. From commercial perspective: NorthBridge is a strategic early customer, we want them to sign but we need to avoid an open-ended damages exposure.

Questions for Legal (Neha):
- Is the 12-month fees cap with express carve-outs for willful misconduct + privacy/data loss defensible?
- Can we keep SLA credits as the exclusive remedy for SLA-type incidents while preserving customer's right to bring other claims for data breaches/gross negligence?

If legal is comfortable, we should present a compromise version to Olivia that narrows the data-loss carve to "direct damages resulting from confirmed loss of Customer Data caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct" and keep a separate line that credits are the sole remedy for SLA performance only.

Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy

Team — reviewed NorthBridge's counter. Proposed compromise (see attached redline_proposed_compromise_neha):

1) Liability cap: set at the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $1,000,000 for each claim, with an annual aggregate cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months. Carve-outs: no cap for liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or proven statutory privacy/data protection violations resulting in regulatory fines.

2) Consequential damages: continue to exclude consequential/indirect losses broadly, BUT add carve to permit recovery of direct losses caused by confirmed loss of Customer Data resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Wording recommended: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover direct damages for documented loss of Customer Data directly caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

3) SLA credits as remedy: accept credits as the exclusive remedy for SLA availability/performance failures only (i.e., limited to performance incidents described in the SLA). Add express language that nothing in the SLA credit sole remedy clause limits Customer's rights arising from data breaches, confidentiality breaches, or Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Rationale: this balances commercial risk (a capped exposure for ordinary service failures) while preserving customer remedies for the most sensitive categories (data/privacy/willful acts). If Product can confirm the SLA metrics and historical availability numbers (cc Rishi), we can present this to NorthBridge.

I attach the tracked compromise redline for negotiation. If NorthBridge insists on fully uncapped liability for data loss, we should push for either: (a) a higher monetary floor, or (b) specific insurance/indemnity commitments and an escalation path to Legal/Finance.

-Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_compromise_redline_neha_20260514.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: cap, consequential carve-outs & SLA credit remedy

Olivia — thanks for the counter and for giving us time to review. We've put together a compromise pass (attached) that we believe protects NorthBridge while keeping liability exposure defined. Key points:

- Cap: greater of fees in prior 12 months or $1M per claim; aggregate cap = prior 12 months' fees.
- Carve-outs: uncapped for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and proven statutory privacy violations.
- Data loss: limited carve allowing recovery of direct damages for documented loss of Customer Data caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- SLA: we will accept credits as the exclusive remedy for SLA availability/performance but that clause will not limit Customer's remedies for data/privacy incidents or gross negligence/willful misconduct.

If this is acceptable, I'll route the redline to DocuSign and we can move to signature. Marcus / Olivia — any objections or alternate language you need us to consider? Happy to set a 20-minute legal-to-legal call if you prefer.

Best —
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
